The present criminal revision has been preferred against the order dated 20.09.2022 passed by the Additional District and Session Judge, Court No. 27 / Special Judge, POCSO Act, Exclusive Court, Agra in Criminal Appeal No. 40 of 2022 (Manish vs. State) as well as order dated 16.05.2022 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Agra arising out of Case Crime No. 164 of 2021, under Sections- 498, 328, 354, 376, 323, 504, 506 IPC and Section of POCSO Act, Police Station- Jagdishpura, District- Agra.

4. After finding the age of revisionist as 16 years, 4 months and 24 days, he was subjected to preliminary assessment as per Section 15 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children)
Act, 2015.

sentences.text:
After calling for a report from Mental Health Hospital, Agra and questioning the revisionist, he was found to be capable of understanding the consequences of his act and was directed to be tried as adult as per order dated 16.05.2022 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board,
Agra.
5.
The Appellate Court has affirmed the same and hence this revision.
6. After considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for the parties, this court finds that the incident in dispute took place on 08.03.2021.
The preliminary assessment of revisionist was ordered by the order dated 29.11.2021 and the report of Mental Health Hospital, Agra was prepared on 24.03.2022.

As per Section 14(3) a preliminary assessment in case of heinous offences under Section 15 is required to be disposed of by the Court within period of three months from the date of first production of child before the Court.
As per only proviso of sub-rule (4) of Section 14 in case of serious or heinous offences, extension of time can be granted by the C.J.M for the reasons to be recorded in writing.
In the present case, there is no such order on record granting extension of time to the Board for conducting preliminary assessment of revisionist after the expiry of period of three months.

7. In Barun Chandra Thakur vs. Bholu reported in 2022 (0) (Supreme) 568 the Apex Court has held that appropriate and specific guidelines with regard to preliminary assessment under Section 15 of J.J. Act, 2015 are not there and had left it open for the Central Government and the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights to consider issuing guidelines or directions in this regard which may assist and facilitate the Board in making the preliminary assessment under section 15 of the Act, 2015, but as yet nothing has been done.
8.

sentences.text: The issue of preliminary assessments of juvenile under Section 15 of J.J. Act is a delicate and difficult task, which requires expertise.
As of now, it is being done in arbitrary manner in absence of any definite parameters/ guidelines for the same.

Therefore this Court deems it appropriate to formulate some guidelines for the Juvenile Justice Board and Children's Court to guide them in making preliminary assessment of juveniles for the purpose of the trial regarding commission of heinous offence as per Section 15 of J.J. Act, 2015, till the legislature formulates appropriate guidelines, as follows:-
GUIDELINES COMPLIANCE X Juvenile vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 7 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163243923/
2

entities.text: GUIDELINES COMPLIANCE X Juvenile vs State Of Up And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (i) The Board will necessarily call the report of psychologist regarding the test of intelligence of child conducted regarding his ability to understand the consequences of his act [like Binet Kamat Test of Intelligence (B.K.T.); Vineland Social Maturity Scale (VSMS); Bhatiya Battery Test of Intelligence or any other test].

The psychologist will indicate in his report clearly what test was performed for assessing mental ability and intelligence of the child so as to ascertain whether he is required to be tried as an adult, who has committed heinous offence.
( iv )

For the reasons given hereinabove, the impugned orders passed by the J.J. Board and the Children's Court are not in accordance with law, hence, the preliminary assessment of the present child in conflict with law requires assessment afresh by J.J. Board within two months as contemplated under section 15(1) of the J.J. Act, 2015.

The assessment of child (revisionist) shall be done on all the parameters/ guidelines stated hereinabove, since the Apex Court in the case of Child in Conflict with Law through his Mother Vs. State of Karnatka, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 798 has held that period of three months provided under Section 14 (3) of the Act for the purpose of conducting psychological test of the child is not mandatory.

10. The order dated 20.09.2022 passed by the Additional District and Session Judge, Court No. 27 /
Special Judge, POCSO Act, Exclusive Court, Agra in Criminal Appeal No. 40 of 2022 (Manish vs.
State) as well as order dated 16.05.2022 passed by the Juvenile Justice Board, Agra are quashed and set aside.
